summary.headline: Mahindra Holidays Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 8% to INR142 crore (34.9% margin) despite a INR234 crore Finland-linked impairment, which wiped out the India books' carrying value of that holding.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 total income was INR407 crore, with operating income up 4.3%, resort income up about 11%, and EBITDA up 8% to INR142 crore (margin +180 bps). A one-off impairment of INR234 crore on the equity investment in a Mauritius entity (linked to the HCRO/Finland business outlook) drove reported standalone PAT down, with PAT ex-one-offs at INR55.4 crore. Consolidated Q4 income rose about 5% to INR844 crore, with EBITDA of INR221 crore (26.2% margin) and PAT ex-one-offs of INR52.3 crore; the European business remained weak on weather, credit rejections and forex. Management reframed FY26 as a transition year, with a shift from member-led growth to resort revenue, non-member sales, Keystone upgrades and a planned portfolio rationalisation.

financial_highlights.value: INR234 crore (equity investment in Mauritius entity)
INR41.5 crore reported; INR52.3 crore ex one-offs

financial_highlights.change: vs INR126 crore in FY25; ~+2% YoY; one-offs mainly Labour Code and forex
Management says it is now growing; prior-year comparison given as INR160 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR93 crore (vs INR56 crore in Q1 of the last four quarters)

segments.name: Standalone India resorts
segments.commentary: Resort income up ~11% in Q4 and 12% for FY26; occupancy at about 80.7-82% and utilisation above 80%, with growth driven by non-member room revenue as member room nights stay flat. Three resorts added in Q4 (Dapoli, North Goa, Chikkamagalur).

segments.name: Europe (HCRO: Finland, Canaries, Sweden)
segments.commentary: Finland hit by no snow for about 1.5 months, a slowdown in the economy, credit rejections on new sales and consumer saving. Canaries and Sweden performed better than last year. Management says FY26 international underperformance splits roughly evenly between forex loss and operational degradation in Finland.

segments.name: Membership and sales (Keystone)
segments.commentary: Keystone launched in December; 1,144 net new members in Q4; referral and digital channels reached 69% of customer acquisition versus 63% a year earlier. The 10-year product is now the largest seller versus the 5-year product previously.

guidance_outlook: Room additions of more than 1,000 keys expected in FY27, after about 900 keys added in FY26 (highest ever); total inventory about 6,228 keys.
Planned upgrades of 300-plus owned keys in FY27; about 100 keys transformed in FY26, with a plan to triple this in FY27.
Portfolio rationalisation (about 500 keys surrendered in FY26) expected to continue for 2-3 quarters, largely complete by end-FY27.

Standalone operating profit trajectory expected to continue, but treasury income may fall in FY27 as capex is deployed. Management says Vision Day target of tripling revenue over the decade is low-teens India growth, not 17-18%.
Signature (first flagship) resort slips from FY27 to FY28. Two to three more locations being prospected. Ganpatipule expected to go live by Q3 FY27.
HCRO strategic review of long-term partnership options to happen in FY27; new credit partners to be onboarded in Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Club Mahindra brand relaunch campaign planned for Q2 or Q3 FY27, with a reasonable increase in marketing spend in those quarters.

Management says the room addition target is unchanged, capital is not a constraint, and only 25-30% of new capacity will be owned, with the rest via capital-light (lease or other) models; occupancy target around 80%.
capex_capacity: About 900 keys added in FY26 (7 managed resorts, same as the prior year; 5 existing-property expansions); more than 1,000 keys planned for FY27.
Three ongoing greenfield or brownfield projects; land bank of about 500 acres; pre-construction started for 5 resorts adding more than 600 keys over the next few years.
Theog (Himachal) and Ganpatipule (Maharashtra) at a decent stage of construction; Ganpatipule to go live by Q3 FY27.
Acquisition of about 50 acres in Chikkamagalur announced on the call date; about 100 acres at Kaas plateau.
Cash of about INR1,446 crore; management says no plans to infuse equity in international operations in the short run.
demand_pricing: Standalone occupancy about 82% in Q4 (management says 80.7-81% utilisation), with membership-led occupancy steady and non-member occupancy growing.
New sales AUR up about 30% (about INR6 lakh) in Q4, held since the December Keystone launch; AUR including upgrades about INR14 lakh.
Upgrades continuing to rise: Q4 upgrade value about INR93 crore versus about INR56 crore in the first quarter of the last four.
Foreign guest exposure described as very small; the model is largely domestic.
Non-member channels (travel agents online and offline, corporate, social and wedding, own website) are separate from the membership sales channel.
Credit rejections on new sales in Europe were high; new lending partners being onboarded.

qa_highlights.question: How did occupancy of about 82% hold up given cancellations and the war environment, and how dependent is the business on foreign guests?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said foreign guest dependency is very small and the model is domestic and member-led; occupancy has historically been high for members and non-members combined, and non-member occupancy keeps growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the sustainability of standalone margin expansion now that marketing and rental savings have been captured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited multiple drivers including cost of acquisition and collection practices. Easier gains are fewer ahead, but resort revenue growth and lower acquisition cost should keep margins improving; treasury income may fall in FY27 as capex rises.

qa_highlights.question: How durable is the AUR uplift, and how much comes from upgrades?
qa_highlights.answer: New-sale AUR is up about 30% and held. Upgrades are rising (Q4 about INR93 crore versus about INR56 crore in Q1), and management expects momentum to continue unless events intervene.

qa_highlights.question: Why did customer acquisition costs not fall with fewer members added, and how is growth in resort revenue achieved with member-to-room ratio below 52?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is managing cost of acquisition as a percentage, not absolute spend; member additions will rise from the last two quarters, not to prior-year levels. Resort revenue growth is mainly room revenue from non-members as the member-to-room ratio improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for HCRO/Finland and why was the impairment taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited consumer saving, weather and credit issues; the impairment reflects the uncertainty prolonging and a new conflict. Two immediate actions: adding credit partners and cost optimisation. A strategic review, including partnerships, is for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are the room addition target and capital-light approach still intact without member-addition cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Room target unchanged; capital is not a constraint. Normalised operating cash flow was above INR300 crore, and only 25-30% of new capacity will be owned, with the rest via lease or other capital-light models; no large debt is planned.

risks_watch: HCRO/Finland: further weakness in sales conversion from credit constraints and consumer saving, with new lending partners not yet onboarded (expected Q1-Q2 FY27).
Forex: net liability exposure on the euro; management says the euro appreciation is largely priced in but may act if a sharp move comes.
Standalone treasury income likely to fall in FY27 as capex rises, which would weigh on reported profit.
Keystone conversion is longer than the older product; sales-team training and referral uptake still settling in. Digital upgrades are only 3-4% of the base.
Signature resort timeline slipped from FY27 to FY28.
Member addition sustainability: management needs to reach the non-member room-filling target while holding guardrails on occupancy (around 80%).

summary.management_tone: Confident on India resorts and Keystone early traction (AUR up ~30%, upgrades rising, occupancy ~80%+), but cautious and non-committal on Europe/HCRO, where management avoided specifics on the strategic review and forex, and gave no timeline beyond FY27. Also flagged the Signature resort slipping to FY28 and treasury income likely falling in FY27.

adds.what: More than 1,000 keys added in FY27 (room additions, mix of owned and capital-light)
Signature flagship resort slipped to FY28
Pre-construction for 5 resorts adding more than 600 keys over next few years

growth.why: Management guides more than 1,000 keys added in FY27 (after about 900 in FY26) and holds the FY30 room-doubling target, with resort income growth of about 11-12% and Ganpatipule live by Q3 FY27; backing is partly specific (named projects, 500 acres, pre-construction on 5 resorts) but Europe is weak and the Signature resort has slipped to FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 34.9% in Q4 (+180 bps) and 36.7% for FY26 vs 31.8% in FY25, with management saying operating profit trajectory continues, though treasury income may fall in FY27 and easy gains are fewer ahead.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 onwards, >1,000 keys in FY27
rows.why: Management expects more than 1,000 keys added in FY27 after about 900 in FY26, with Ganpatipule going live by Q3 FY27, but Signature has slipped to FY28 and Europe is weak.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone resort income up about 11% in Q4 and 12% for FY26, with occupancy at about 80.7-82% and non-member room revenue growing, while member room nights are flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 80.7% is at the high end, about 2 projects under construction, 500 acres land bank, pre-construction on 5 resorts with more than 600 keys, and Chikkamagalur 50-acre acquisition announced on the call, with cash of about INR1,446 crore and capital not a constraint.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is not raising guidance; the Vision Day target was reframed to low-teens India growth rather than 17-18%, and Europe remains weak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Treasury income likely to fall in FY27 as capex is deployed, Signature slipped from FY27 to FY28, and Europe credit rejections and forex are unresolved, with new credit partners only onboarded in Q1-Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Club Mahindra brand relaunch campaign planned for Q2 or Q3 FY27 with higher marketing spend, and Keystone (launched December) is already the largest seller, with AUR up about 30% to about INR6 lakh on new sales.

rows.label: New-sale AUR uplift held at ~30%
rows.why: New-sale AUR is up about 30% to about INR6 lakh since the December Keystone launch and has held; AUR including upgrades is about INR14 lakh.

rows.label: Upgrade value rising
rows.why: Q4 upgrade value was about INR93 crore vs about INR56 crore in Q1 of the prior four quarters (+33% YoY), and planned upgrades of 300-plus owned keys in FY27 are about three times FY26's ~100 keys.

rows.label: HCRO strategic review and new credit partners
rows.when: H1 FY27 for partners; strategic review in FY27
rows.why: New credit partners to be onboarded in Q1-Q2 FY27 and a strategic review of partnership options is due in FY27, after Finland's weak sales and credit rejections, with no timeline beyond FY27 given.

tone.note: Management was confident on India resorts, Keystone traction, AUR (+30%) and upgrades, but cautious and non-committal on Europe/HCRO, forex, and the strategic review timeline; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, AUR durability, customer acquisition costs and the HCRO plan.
